name: Baseline
description: Endogenous fast-transition baseline: model defaults with 2025-level carbon prices and no further policy. After the 2026 accounting reconciliation and the round-2 efficiency-series coupling (production eta and demand intensity decline are one series, with the structural/catch-up component decaying post-2025), the no-policy path is: GDP growth ~2.8%/yr to 2050 decelerating to ~2.6%/yr, 2050 generation ~83k TWh (~1.5x IEA STEPS ~55k — faster because Way-et-al learning keeps solar+storage undercutting fossil), near-term electricity growth ~3-4%/yr (IEA actual), fossil electricity ~9% in 2050 falling to ~0 by 2075, warming ~2.6C by 2100 (AR6-consistent marginal TCRE). GDP 2100 ~$1,150T sits between the SSP2 (~$700T) and SSP5 (~$1,240T) markers, 2017 PPP. NOTE: the GDP LEVEL is the model's weakest output — it is dominated by serviceEfficiencyGrowth, a soft residual whose plausible range spans GDP 2100 ~$0.8-1.4Q (see docs/SENSITIVITY.md); read the level as a band, the transition shape as robust. Not a replication of any IEA scenario.
